land.text: the mainland, retaken by Ruffo's Sanfedists (Naples on 13 June 1799; Pescara, the last stronghold, on 30 June); Ferdinand re-entered the Bay of Naples on 10 July 1799

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; the Kingdom of Naples (Napoleonic) row, 1762 shape, is the outline used). The republic covered 'the former kingdom's territory' on the mainland; the page gives no area and says only that it 'divided the former kingdom's territory into departments', with Abruzzo and Pescara named and Calabria the royalist base. The extent in the south is therefore uncertain.

ledger.note: 21-23 January 1799: the Parthenopean Republic is proclaimed at Naples. 'On 21 or 23 January 1799, the Parthenopean Republic was proclaimed'; after the republicans took Castel Sant'Elmo on 20 January 'the French entered the city the next day'. 'The republic existed from 21 January to 13 June 1799.'

region.text: the former kingdom's mainland territory, which the republic 'divided ... into departments'

ledger.note: 13 June 1799: Ruffo's Sanfedists retake Naples. 'On 13 June 1799. Ruffo and his troops reached Naples' and fought their way in; the republic collapsed 'when the Sanfedists returned Ferdinand to power' (he 'entered the Bay of Naples' on 10 July 1799). The castles of Sant'Elmo, Nuovo and dell'Ovo still held out; Pescara, 'the last Jacobin stronghold', surrendered on 30 June 1799.

region.text: the former kingdom's mainland territory, which the republic 'divided ... into departments'

ledger.note: 13 June 1799: the Parthenopean Republic ends after about five months.

wars.name: Sanfedist reconquest of the Kingdom of Naples

zones.text: the former kingdom's mainland territory, which the republic 'divided ... into departments'

wars.outcome: Cardinal Ruffo raised a 'Christian army' in Calabria, reached Naples on 13 June 1799 and ended the republic; Pescara fell on 30 June; Ferdinand returned on 10 July 1799.
wars.note: The page gives the dates of the endgame only; the spring advance through the provinces is not dated.

certainty.note: The republic's real authority outside Naples and Abruzzo (the places the page names) is not given by the page; Calabria was a royalist base.

sources.title: Parthenopean Republic
sources.note: Proclamation 21 or 23 January 1799, existence to 13 June 1799, Ruffo's reconquest, Pescara 30 June, Ferdinand's return 10 July.

notes: New dossier, a state Cliopatria lacks. The kingdom-of-naples-bourbon dossier already carries the matching loss (January) and gain (June) against the slug 'parthenopean-republic'. One page opened (budget for a state of five months). It gives no area; the mainland of the Kingdom of Naples (Cliopatria's 1762 shape without Sicily) is the outline, which probably overstates a republic whose hold on Calabria, the royalist base, was weak. The proclamation date is the page's 'either 21 or 23 January'; the page's French entry is 21 January.
